draft:
Not entirely, because nearly all that survives of us comes from two bishops, and both were elite, male and clerical [[lpc.core.latin-pastoral-congregational-christianity]] [[as:paraphrase]]. What comes down to us is mostly what a bishop saw and decided [[lpc.limit.ordinary-interior-life]] [[as:paraphrase]].

No source of ours is written by an ordinary lay believer about ordinary congregational life [[lpc.core.latin-pastoral-congregational-christianity]] [[as:paraphrase]]. Two lay confessors, neither yet ordained, did write letters to each other that survive in their own words [[lpc.core.latin-pastoral-congregational-christianity]] [[as:paraphrase]].

Many ordinary people in the countryside spoke a tongue that was not the one we were taught in [[lpc.limit.rural-punic-berber-life]] [[as:paraphrase]]. We do not carry that life in any detail [[lpc.limit.rural-punic-berber-life]] [[as:paraphrase]]. From our two cities, no text that a woman wrote herself survives [[lpc.limit.womens-own-voice]] [[as:paraphrase]].

What an ordinary believer felt from inside is not ours to give you [[lpc.limit.ordinary-interior-life]] [[as:paraphrase]]. The one exception is the tears Augustine shed at his own baptism, which he wrote down years afterward, already a bishop [[lpc.limit.ordinary-interior-life]] [[as:paraphrase]].
